currentContext.business: Quess Corp provides customised workforce management, staffing and recruitment solutions - General Staffing for high-volume talent acquisition and deployment across industries, Professional Staffing offering integrated IT staffing across verticals, an Overseas Business serving clients across the Asia-Pacific and Middle East regions, and Digital Platforms covering talent acquisition, executive search and recruitment, payroll compliance and end-to-end manpower management. The Company operates at the intersection of employment generation, workforce formalisation, compliance management and technology-enabled human capital solutions, serving sectors including BFSI, retail, telecom, manufacturing, IT, GCCs and construction. Following the completion of its demerger in FY25, the Company reports on a post-demerger basis covering Quess Corp Limited and its subsidiaries.

currentContext.strengths: Management's stated positioning for labour-code-driven formalisation: 'The Company's scale, compliance infrastructure, digital systems, and experience in managing large associate workforces position it well to benefit from the formalisation trend.'|India's largest staffing and workforce solutions provider, delivering technology-driven staffing and managed outsourcing through deep domain expertise and AI-enabled digital platforms|Low customer concentration - none of the Group's customers accounts for revenue of more than 10.00% of total Group revenue|Diversification across four service lines (General Staffing, Professional Staffing, Overseas Business, Digital Platforms) and multiple geographies, supported by a wholly-owned international subsidiary network across Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Sri Lanka and the Middle East|Long-standing relationships with leading enterprises, positioning the Company for niche technology hiring and integrated workforce solutions for global enterprises establishing or scaling India capability centres
currentContext.strategies: Three stated priorities for the next phase of growth: enabling Global Capability Centers (GCCs), accelerating the adoption of AI and technology, and expanding presence across global talent corridors|Enable the GCC ecosystem - leverage workforce expertise and an active client base of over 140 GCCs to help global enterprises find, manage and grow talent in India|Invest in AI across the business - from sourcing and screening to payroll, employee engagement and redeployment - to simplify processes, improve productivity and improve client and associate experience|Build structured global talent corridors connecting India's surplus workforce with global demand, supported by expanding infrastructure for language training, international certification and compliant mobilisation|Build deeper where India has structural advantage, expand selectively where global demand is strong, and use technology to make the operating model sharper, faster and more resilient|Post-demerger singular focus on workforce solutions as a people-only business|Continue to invest in people and technology, deepen customer relationships, improve productivity and maintain disciplined capital allocation|Strengthen leadership and succession - build leadership from within and strengthen the internal mentoring pipeline; Board evolved post-demerger with independent directors bringing global, financial and sectoral perspective|Shareholder distributions are governed by a stated Dividend Distribution Policy. For FY 2025-26 an interim dividend was paid on the equity shares and is placed before the 19th AGM for confirmation, with a final dividend for the year carrying a record date of Friday, August 07, 2026. No amount was proposed to be transferred to reserves during the year under review, with earnings retained in the business rather than appropriated to reserves. Unpaid or unclaimed dividends, and the shares on which dividends remain unclaimed for seven consecutive years, are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund in accordance with Section 124(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 and the IEPF Rules; during the year under review there were no unclaimed dividends or corresponding shares due to be transferred, and shareholders are encouraged to review their records and claim past dividends.|ESG philosophy 'What's good for society is good for Quess', anchored on four strategic pillars: The People Company, Responsible Citizen, Environmentally Conscious, and Trusted Institution|Environmental: promotion of paperless operations through digital workflows to reduce paper consumption and lower the environmental footprint|Environmental: responsible resource and waste management - segregation of paper and food waste, energy-efficient lighting fixtures, and adherence to municipal guidelines for water sourcing and disposal|Social: mobilising talent and expanding access to formal employment, supporting the transition of workers into the formal economy with access to social security and structured employment|Social: digital job discovery through platforms such as QJobs and Monster; vocational training, skilling and employability enhancement through partnerships and training centres across India|Social: employee wellbeing, engagement and career development, and diversity and inclusion across workforce categories|CSR delivered through Careworks Foundation, focused on quality education, healthcare, clean water, sanitation and community development (CSR applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013)|Governance: Code of Conduct, anti-bribery and anti-corruption practices, whistle-blower mechanism, information security and data privacy management, and continuous strengthening of cyber security and compliance processes|Governance: Enterprise Risk Management framework aligned with COSO and ISO 31000, with enterprise risk oversight by the Risk Management & ESG Committee of the Board, supported by Internal Audit and designated risk owners|ESG strategy, implementation and monitoring overseen by the Risk Management & ESG Committee; ESG disclosures published through the Sustainability Report and Business Responsibility Report|Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for all stakeholder groups; all 8 shareholder complaints filed in FY 2025-26 were resolved and closed|New Labour Code implementation identified in the BRSR materiality table as an opportunity with positive financial implication, with system and policy enhancements completed pending formal notification of state-specific rules
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or physical capex programme - Quess is an asset-light workforce-solutions business and expansion is described in terms of capability, technology and geographic footprint rather than commissioning timelines. The Chairman frames the next phase of growth around three expansion vectors: enabling Global Capability Centers (GCCs), accelerating the adoption of AI and technology, and expanding presence across global talent corridors. On GCCs, management notes that more than 2,000 GCCs operate in India today and the number is expected to exceed 2,500 by 2030, with Quess already serving an active client base of over 140 GCCs and preparing to help these organisations find, manage and grow talent. On technology, the Company states it is investing in AI across the business - from sourcing and screening to payroll, employee engagement and redeployment - with the aim of simplifying processes, improving productivity and improving the client and associate experience. On geography, global talent mobility is described as one of the most significant long-term opportunities, driven by ageing populations and widening skill gaps in advanced economies against India's young, increasingly mobile workforce. No project names, capex amounts, site additions or commissioning/ramp dates are disclosed in these sections.
currentContext.mdna: GCC expansion in India is the core demand driver - more than 2,000 GCCs operate in India today and the number is expected to exceed 2,500 by 2030; contractual roles are expected to account for nearly one in four GCC roles by 2026 versus 18% in 2024|IT flexi staffing demand is strengthening - industry employment grew 10.1% year-on-year in FY26, supported by GCC expansion, rising enterprise technology spending and wider adoption of AI-enabled business models|General staffing grew nearly 7.9% year-on-year in FY26, with the formal flexi workforce crossing 1.9 million associates|Implementation of the four Labour Codes is viewed as structurally positive - consolidation of 29 legacy laws, with formalisation projected to rise from 60.4% to 75.5%, favouring organised players with scale and compliance infrastructure|Near-term headwind: Labour Code implementation affected revenue recognition in the General Staffing segment during FY26|Near-term headwind: a softer hiring environment in certain sectors driven by macroeconomic uncertainty and rapid technological change|Demand diversification beyond BFSI/retail/telecom into manufacturing, logistics, infrastructure, healthcare and e-commerce - bringing longer engagement cycles, higher workforce intensity, more stable demand and improved margin potential|Mix shift from a fulfilment-led, scale-driven general staffing model to a solution-oriented, capability-led, data-driven workforce optimisation model ('from scale to smart scale')|AI as both disruption and opportunity - creating demand for AI upskilling and AI governance roles while improving candidate matching speed, time-to-deploy and fulfilment rates; Quess has flagged AI-led initiatives in Professional Staffing|Rise of blended gig/hybrid workforce models and platformisation of staffing services, driving demand for integrated workforce solutions and enabling scale without proportional operational complexity|Government employment initiatives (ELI / PMVBRY) expected to improve the competitiveness of organised staffing models over informal structures|India macro backdrop supportive - FY26 real GDP growth around 7.6%, IMF projecting around 6.5% for FY27, with services expanding around 7.5-7.8%|Global staffing market (SIA estimate roughly US$650-700 billion) has been broadly flat for two years; Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region at 7-8% annually to 2030|Management flagged threats of client insourcing, macroeconomic/geopolitical uncertainty, competitive intensity and pricing pressure in General Staffing, and overseas regulatory change (Singapore COMPASS, Middle East localisation)

risks.note: Staffing and workforce management is sensitive to economic cycles, business sentiment and hiring trends; slowdowns in manufacturing, retail, IT services, BFSI, logistics or global trade can directly reduce workforce deployment and hiring demand. Mitigated by a diversified portfolio across sectors, workforce categories and geographies and by an asset-light, technology-enabled operating structure.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk (labour laws, wages, social security, immigration)
risks.note: The business operates in a highly regulated environment spanning labour laws, wage regulations, social security compliance, taxation and immigration policies across multiple jurisdictions; regulatory change can alter operating models and raise compliance costs. The Company also flags potential non-compliance risk on the new Labour Codes, including incorporating revised requirements into payroll systems and increased financial exposure from changed wage structures and social security obligations - while treating the Codes as a net opportunity versus unorganised players.

Growth depends on attracting, deploying, engaging and retaining workforce across blue-collar, grey-collar, professional and gig categories; higher attrition and competition for skilled talent can impair operational efficiency and service delivery. Attrition is structurally high - permanent worker turnover was 115.2% in FY 2025-26 and permanent employee turnover 50.8%, both above the prior year.

As a technology-driven staffing organisation operating proprietary platforms handling large volumes of associate, candidate and client data, the Company is exposed to ransomware, system intrusions and data breaches; a compromise could disrupt operations, expose sensitive data and cause financial, reputational, regulatory and legal consequences. Mitigations include a Cyber Security Council led by the CTO and Business IT Heads, ISO-aligned practices, periodic VAPT, DLP, 2FA, WAF, MDM and endpoint security, and a centralised network/firewall/log-monitoring architecture across offices.

risks.risk: Client concentration and competitive intensity / pricing pressure
risks.note: The staffing industry is highly competitive with increasing pricing pressure, evolving service expectations and technology-led disruption; loss of key clients or sustained pricing pressure can hit profitability and market positioning. Countered through integrated workforce solutions, a diversified client base, long-standing relationships and higher-value offerings such as GCC staffing, managed services and AI-enabled workforce solutions.

International staffing operations are exposed to geopolitical developments, local regulatory change, visa restrictions, currency fluctuations and region-specific labour market risks across APAC and Middle Eastern markets. Mitigated by geographic diversification, continuous evaluation of country-specific regulatory environments, local operational expertise and flexible deployment strategies.

As the digital ecosystem expands, sustained adoption and engagement across associates, gig workers and enterprise clients is critical for platform scalability and monetisation; the Company relies on platforms such as Hamara HR, Hamara Jobs and TaskMo for workforce engagement and scalable service delivery.

Managing a workforce base of significant scale across geographies, sectors and client locations carries risks around deployment efficiency, service quality, productivity and execution consistency; addressed with technology-led workforce management systems, AI-enabled automation, standardised operating procedures and real-time monitoring.

As a large workforce management organisation, gaps in employee welfare, compliance, ethical practices or stakeholder engagement could damage brand reputation and stakeholder trust; workplace safety is separately identified as a material issue where failure to maintain a safe and healthy work environment may result in accidents, injuries or misconduct.

one-line thesis: Quess Corp delivered a structural inflection in Q4FY26 with consolidated EBITDA margins expanding 37bps YoY to 2.2%, driven by a deliberate portfolio shift where high-margin businesses (Professional & Overseas) now contribute 50% of profitability despite muted top-line growth. The key takeaway is the sustainability of double-digit margins in Professional Staffing (12%) and the successful navigation of regulatory headwinds (Labor Code) while maintaining a net-cash balance sheet and initiating special dividends.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 3,892cr (+6% YoY); EBITDA: INR 86cr (+28% YoY, 2.2% margin); PAT: INR 64cr (+167% YoY reported, adjusted stable); Order Book: N/A (Staffing model); Net Debt: Negative INR 271cr (Net Cash). One-offs: Q3 included one-time gratuity billing pass-through due to Labor Code causing Q4 sequential revenue dip; FY26 included exit of low-margin milestone project (7k headcount, ~INR 200cr revenue impact).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting 10-11% headcount growth and 12-13% revenue growth in FY27 for Professional Staffing; General Staffing aiming to utilize 50% idle capacity to return to historical addition rates. Margins: Consolidated baseline established at >2%, targeting 2.4% medium-term; Professional Staffing sustained at 11-12%; Overseas sustained at >6%. Order Inflow: 275-300 new logos/year capacity in General Staffing; 61 new logos added in Professional Staffing FY26.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (revenue recognized on time-and-materials/monthly billing); however, active contract pipeline includes 281 new contracts in General Staffing and 61 new logos in Professional Staffing added in FY26, with 50% of new Professional logos already active.
segment / subsidiary detail: General Staffing: Rev INR 3,328cr (Q4), EBITDA INR 52cr (+21% YoY), Margin 1.5%. Headcount net add 26k (offset by 7k discontinuation). Professional Staffing: Rev INR 232cr (Q4), EBITDA INR 30cr (+47% YoY), Margin ~12.7%. GCC mix 71%. Overseas: Rev INR 332cr (Q4, +16% YoY), EBITDA INR 21cr (+18% YoY), Margin >6%. Middle East margin 11%, Philippines 10%.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling Professional Staffing into niche AI/Cyber/Data roles (60% of demand vs 30% two years ago); expanding Overseas footprint in Malaysia (83% rev growth) and Philippines; leveraging AI-driven blue-collar marketplace to improve General Staffing yield; capturing untapped capacity in General Staffing sales team (currently operating at 50% of installed capacity).
margins & cost dynamics: Margin expansion driven by mix shift (50% profit from high-margin segments), exit of low-yield engagements, and pricing discipline. Cost side managed via technology investments in recruitment; Labor Code implementation caused temporary billing distortions (gratuity pass-through) but no permanent cost inflation confirmed yet.
capex / expansion: Investment-focused on digital platforms, AI-led recruitment tools, and verticalization of sales teams. No heavy physical capex; operating model remains asset-light.
capital allocation: Net cash position of INR 271cr with zero gross debt. Board approved Final Dividend INR 3/share + Special Dividend INR 3/share (10th IPO anniversary). Payout aligned with free cash flow generation while maintaining liquidity for growth.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability in Middle East (though portfolio diversified in essential services); Regulatory uncertainty around final Labor Code rules notification (expected Q1-Q2 FY27); Potential GCC hiring slowdown due to AI automation (mitigated by shift to high-experience niche roles); Supply-side talent shrinkage in India.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'quality of earnings' over volume; transparent about one-off discontinuations; bullish on structural margin sustainability rather than cyclical spikes.
non-obvious takeaways: The 7,000 headcount discontinuation was a conscious strategic exit of a milestone-based project with poor cash realization, removing ~INR 200cr revenue but improving overall ROE; General Staffing is currently running at only 50% of its sales/recruitment installed capacity due to macro headwinds, implying significant latent operating leverage if demand normalizes in FY27.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Increased demand for niche, experienced tech talent (7-8+ years) in AI, Cloud, Cyber Security as GCCs shift from volume to value | Quess Corp Limited | beneficiary | High | Company has structurally pivoted Professional Staffing to 71% GCC mix with 60% demand in emerging tech, commanding 12%+ margins vs industry average; competitors stuck in low-end volume staffing may lose share. |
| Labor Code implementation creating billing confusion and potential cost pass-through delays for pure-play low-margin staffing firms | Unorganized/Small Staffing Peers | loser | Med | Quess has already navigated Q3/Q4 billing distortions and has scale to absorb compliance costs; smaller players may face cash flow crunches due to inability to pass through gratuity/benefits costs efficiently. |

hero.oneLiner: Quess Corp is India's leading workforce management company and one of the largest integrated staffing and employment solutions platforms in the region, headquartered in Bengaluru.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Quess Corp is India's leading workforce management company and one of the largest integrated staffing and employment solutions platforms in the region, headquartered in Bengaluru.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Quess Corp provides customised workforce management, staffing and recruitment solutions - General Staffing for high-volume talent acquisition and deployment across industries, Professional Staffing offering integrated IT staffing across verticals, an Overseas Business serving clients across the Asia-Pacific and Middle East regions, and Digital Platforms covering talent acquisition, executive search and recruitment, payroll compliance and end-to-end manpower management. The Company operates at the intersection of employment generation, workforce formalisation, compliance management and technology-enabled human capital solutions, serving sectors including BFSI, retail, telecom, manufacturing, IT, GCCs and construction. Following the completion of its demerger in FY25, the Company reports on a post-demerger basis covering Quess Corp Limited and its subsidiaries.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: General Staffing: Rev INR 3,328cr (Q4), EBITDA INR 52cr (+21% YoY), Margin 1.5%. Headcount net add 26k (offset by 7k discontinuation). Professional Staffing: Rev INR 232cr (Q4), EBITDA INR 30cr (+47% YoY), Margin ~12.7%. GCC mix 71%. Overseas: Rev INR 332cr (Q4, +16% YoY), EBITDA INR 21cr (+18% YoY), Margin >6%. Middle East margin 11%, Philippines 10%.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **General Staffing:** Customised workforce management and recruitment solutions, Specialised talent acquisition and deployment services tailored to client needs
- **Professional Staffing:** Integrated IT staffing solutions across a broad spectrum of industry verticals, Specialised talent acquisition and workforce deployment services
- **Overseas Business:** Staffing and recruitment solutions for clients across Asia-Pacific and the Middle East
- **Digital Platforms:** Customised staffing services, Talent acquisition, Executive search and recruitment, Payroll compliance, End-to-end manpower management solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (domestic; exports less than 1% of standalone turnover)
- Asia-Pacific
- Middle East - Saudi Arabia, UAE and Qatar (infrastructure-led demand for general and specialist staffing)
- Singapore (affected by the COMPASS framework tightening foreign work pass approvals)
- Malaysia and the Philippines (expanding services sectors and digital economy)
- BFSI
- Retail
- Telecom
- Manufacturing
- IT services and Global Capability Centres (GCCs)
- Construction

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (revenue recognized on time-and-materials/monthly billing); however, active contract pipeline includes 281 new contracts in General Staffing and 61 new logos in Professional Staffing added in FY26, with 50% of new Professional logos already active.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting 10-11% headcount growth and 12-13% revenue growth in FY27 for Professional Staffing; General Staffing aiming to utilize 50% idle capacity to return to historical addition rates. Margins: Consolidated baseline established at >2%, targeting 2.4% medium-term; Professional Staffing sustained at 11-12%; Overseas sustained at >6%. Order Inflow: 275-300 new logos/year capacity in General Staffing; 61 new logos added in Professional Staffing FY26.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Scaling Professional Staffing into niche AI/Cyber/Data roles (60% of demand vs 30% two years ago); expanding Overseas footprint in Malaysia (83% rev growth) and Philippines; leveraging AI-driven blue-collar marketplace to improve General Staffing yield; capturing untapped capacity in General Staffing sales team (currently operating at 50% of installed capacity).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- GCC expansion in India is the core demand driver - more than 2,000 GCCs operate in India today and the number is expected to exceed 2,500 by 2030; contractual roles are expected to account for nearly one in four GCC roles by 2026 versus 18% in 2024
- IT flexi staffing demand is strengthening - industry employment grew 10.1% year-on-year in FY26, supported by GCC expansion, rising enterprise technology spending and wider adoption of AI-enabled business models
- General staffing grew nearly 7.9% year-on-year in FY26, with the formal flexi workforce crossing 1.9 million associates
- Implementation of the four Labour Codes is viewed as structurally positive - consolidation of 29 legacy laws, with formalisation projected to rise from 60.4% to 75.5%, favouring organised players with scale and compliance infrastructure
- Near-term headwind: Labour Code implementation affected revenue recognition in the General Staffing segment during FY26
- Near-term headwind: a softer hiring environment in certain sectors driven by macroeconomic uncertainty and rapid technological change
- Demand diversification beyond BFSI/retail/telecom into manufacturing, logistics, infrastructure, healthcare and e-commerce - bringing longer engagement cycles, higher workforce intensity, more stable demand and improved margin potential
- Mix shift from a fulfilment-led, scale-driven general staffing model to a solution-oriented, capability-led, data-driven workforce optimisation model ('from scale to smart scale')
- AI as both disruption and opportunity - creating demand for AI upskilling and AI governance roles while improving candidate matching speed, time-to-deploy and fulfilment rates; Quess has flagged AI-led initiatives in Professional Staffing
- Rise of blended gig/hybrid workforce models and platformisation of staffing services, driving demand for integrated workforce solutions and enabling scale without proportional operational complexity
- Government employment initiatives (ELI / PMVBRY) expected to improve the competitiveness of organised staffing models over informal structures
- India macro backdrop supportive - FY26 real GDP growth around 7.6%, IMF projecting around 6.5% for FY27, with services expanding around 7.5-7.8%
- Global staffing market (SIA estimate roughly US$650-700 billion) has been broadly flat for two years; Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region at 7-8% annually to 2030
- Management flagged threats of client insourcing, macroeconomic/geopolitical uncertainty, competitive intensity and pricing pressure in General Staffing, and overseas regulatory change (Singapore COMPASS, Middle East localisation)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin expansion driven by mix shift (50% profit from high-margin segments), exit of low-yield engagements, and pricing discipline. Cost side managed via technology investments in recruitment; Labor Code implementation caused temporary billing distortions (gratuity pass-through) but no permanent cost inflation confirmed yet.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position of INR 271cr with zero gross debt. Board approved Final Dividend INR 3/share + Special Dividend INR 3/share (10th IPO anniversary). Payout aligned with free cash flow generation while maintaining liquidity for growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or physical capex programme - Quess is an asset-light workforce-solutions business and expansion is described in terms of capability, technology and geographic footprint rather than commissioning timelines. The Chairman frames the next phase of growth around three expansion vectors: enabling Global Capability Centers (GCCs), accelerating the adoption of AI and technology, and expanding presence across global talent corridors. On GCCs, management notes that more than 2,000 GCCs operate in India today and the number is expected to exceed 2,500 by 2030, with Quess already serving an active client base of over 140 GCCs and preparing to help these organisations find, manage and grow talent. On technology, the Company states it is investing in AI across the business - from sourcing and screening to payroll, employee engagement and redeployment - with the aim of simplifying processes, improving productivity and improving the client and associate experience. On geography, global talent mobility is described as one of the most significant long-term opportunities, driven by ageing populations and widening skill gaps in advanced economies against India's young, increasingly mobile workforce. No project names, capex amounts, site additions or commissioning/ramp dates are disclosed in these sections.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'quality of earnings' over volume; transparent about one-off discontinuations; bullish on structural margin sustainability rather than cyclical spikes.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Management's stated positioning for labour-code-driven formalisation: 'The Company's scale, compliance infrastructure, digital systems, and experience in managing large associate workforces position it well to benefit from the formalisation trend.'
- India's largest staffing and workforce solutions provider, delivering technology-driven staffing and managed outsourcing through deep domain expertise and AI-enabled digital platforms
- Low customer concentration - none of the Group's customers accounts for revenue of more than 10.00% of total Group revenue
- Diversification across four service lines (General Staffing, Professional Staffing, Overseas Business, Digital Platforms) and multiple geographies, supported by a wholly-owned international subsidiary network across Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Sri Lanka and the Middle East
- Long-standing relationships with leading enterprises, positioning the Company for niche technology hiring and integrated workforce solutions for global enterprises establishing or scaling India capability centres

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical instability in Middle East (though portfolio diversified in essential services); Regulatory uncertainty around final Labor Code rules notification (expected Q1-Q2 FY27); Potential GCC hiring slowdown due to AI automation (mitigated by shift to high-experience niche roles); Supply-side talent shrinkage in India.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 7,000 headcount discontinuation was a conscious strategic exit of a milestone-based project with poor cash realization, removing ~INR 200cr revenue but improving overall ROE; General Staffing is currently running at only 50% of its sales/recruitment installed capacity due to macro headwinds, implying significant latent operating leverage if demand normalizes in FY27.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Three stated priorities for the next phase of growth: enabling Global Capability Centers (GCCs), accelerating the adoption of AI and technology, and expanding presence across global talent corridors
- Enable the GCC ecosystem - leverage workforce expertise and an active client base of over 140 GCCs to help global enterprises find, manage and grow talent in India
- Invest in AI across the business - from sourcing and screening to payroll, employee engagement and redeployment - to simplify processes, improve productivity and improve client and associate experience
- Build structured global talent …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Increased demand for niche, experienced tech talent (7-8+ years) in AI, Cloud, Cyber Security as GCCs shift from volume to value | Quess Corp Limited | beneficiary | High | Company has structurally pivoted Professional Staffing to 71% GCC mix with 60% demand in emerging tech, commanding 12%+ margins vs industry average; competitors stuck in low-end volume staffing may lose share. |
| Labor Code implementation creating billing confusion and potential cost pass-through delays for pure-play low-margin staffing firms | Unorganized/Small Staffing Peers | loser | Med | Quess has already navigated Q3/Q4 billing distortions and has scale to absorb compliance costs; smaller players may face cash flow crunches due to inability to pass through gratuity/benefits costs efficiently. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] A 3-way demerger completed in the 2025-onwards phase reset Quess into a focused staffing play — simplified corporate structure, enhanced management focus and clarity of investment thesis.
- [Regulation] India's new Labour Code changed revenue recognition, producing a one-time revenue increase of ₹176 crore in the quarter within General Staffing.
- [Market] The India staffing & recruitment market is projected to grow from $19Bn (2022) to $49Bn (2030) at ~13% CAGR, with the flexi workforce growing 12.6% CAGR to 9.16Mn by FY27; Quess holds ~26% share of the 1.8Mn ISF flexi headcount.
- [Ownership] Promoters hold 56.9% with Ajit Isaac as founder and Non-Executive Chairman; Fairfax Financial Holdings (2013 investment) is described as the largest shareholder to date, and notable public holders include Tata Mutual Fund 7.86% and Ashish Dhawan 4.90%.
- [Governance] Board of 8 directors of whom 4 (50%) are independent, with a Non-Executive Chairman and a single Executive Director; CMMI Level 3 certified in 2026.
